The species $P, Q, R$ and $S$ respectively are

solution.text: Given reactions are $[P] \stackrel{\mathrm{Br}_{2}}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{4} \mathrm{Br}_{2} \frac{\mathrm{NaNH}_{2}}{\mathrm{NH}_{3}},[Q]$ $[Q] \frac{20 \% / \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}}{\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}, \Delta},[\mathrm{R}] \stackrel{\mathrm{Zn} \cdot \mathrm{Hg} / \mathrm{HG}}{\longrightarrow}[S]$ $[P]$ is an alkene with two carbon atoms i.e. ethene. When it reacts with Br $y$, addition reaction occurs and $\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{4} \mathrm{Br}_{2}$ is formed. $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{H}}, \mathrm{Br}_{2}$(1, 2-dibromoethane) on reaction with $\operatorname{NaNH}_{2} / \mathrm{NH},$ gives ethyne $(\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{H}, \mathrm{y})$ Ethyne IQlin presence of $20 \% \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{SO}_{4}, \mathrm{Hg}^{2+} \mathrm{at} 333 \mathrm{K}$ gives ethanal. Ethanal $[R]$ undergoes reduction in presence of $$ \text { Zn-Hg /HCl to give ethane }[S] $$ $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CHO} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{HCl}]{\mathrm{Zn-Hg}} \mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$
